item.title: N.H. girls soccer: Arico hat trick sends Portsmouth Christian back to Division IV final
item.description: LACONIA – The Portsmouth Christian Academy girls soccer team will get a chance to defend its Division IV state championship. The top-seeded Eagles scored four times in the opening 40 minutes and rolled into a second straight championship game with a 5-0 semifinal win over No. 5 Profile on Tuesday, Nov. 3 at Laconia High School. Tilly Arico led the the Eagles with a hat trick, while Sylvie Wamberg had a goal and two assists, and Sophie Anderson had one goal. The Eagles (17-1) led 4-0 at halftime and wasted little time putting the game away after the break, scoring approximately two minutes into the second half. With a five-goal advantage, PCA coach Derek Summers was able to turn to his bench for much of the remaining time. “I would say I knew if we played well, there was a chance of that, and we played well tonight,” Summers said. The victory earned Portsmouth Christian a spot in Friday's Division IV championship game against No. 2 Groveton (14-2-2) at 5 p.m. at Laconia High School. Groveton advanced with a 2-1 semifinal win over No. 6 Gorham. “I am happy to have the opportunity to defend our championship on Friday night," Summers said. "(Groveton's) goalie looked really, really good (against Gorham). She played really well. They have a lot of speed, and a couple wingers that are really fast.” Eagles continue dominant run The Eagles' offense provided more than enough support Tuesday, but their defense was just as impressive. Center backs Brie Mullins and Ruthie Sherrill helped keep Profile from generating scoring opportunities. “Honestly, my center backs were great,” Summers said. The shutout continued an impressive run for PCA since its only loss of the season, which came against Mount Royal Academy on Oct. 5. Portsmouth Christian has since won 10 straight games, outscoring the opposition, 60-4. A return to the championship game isn't necessarily a surprise for a PCA team that returned significant talent from last year's title-winning squad. “Yes, I would say that we did expect that,” Summers said. “I only had two seniors on the team last year. We have a lot of talent.” This article originally appeared on Portsmouth Herald: N.H. girls soccer: Arico hat trick sends Portsmouth Christian back to Division IV final

item.title: Lightning’s Brandon Hagel Takes Shot at Dylan Larkin Amid Trade Drama
item.description: The Dylan Larkin trade saga has already created plenty of controversy in Detroit, and now a player from one of the Red Wings’ biggest division rivals appears to be taking a shot at the former captain. Tampa Bay Lightning forward Brandon Hagel made some interesting comments Monday while discussing teammate Nikita Kucherov’s request to be traded. And although Hagel never mentioned Larkin by name, his comparison certainly sounded familiar to anyone following the situation in Hockeytown. The timing makes the comments even more interesting, with Detroit and Tampa Bay scheduled to square off Tuesday night. But while explaining why Kucherov’s situation is different from other players seeking trades, Hagel delivered a pointed remark. “It’s not like he committed here for eight years and asked out, two years into it. This is a different situation,” Hagel said during Monday’s media availability . Sound like anybody familiar? Larkin signed an eight-year, $69.6 million contract extension with Detroit in March 2023. He subsequently requested a trade during the 2026 offseason and was suspended without pay last week after informing the organization that he would no longer play until a deal was completed. Hagel did not specifically identify Larkin, so there is no way to establish with certainty that the Red Wings center was his intended target. However, the similarities are difficult to ignore, particularly with the two Atlantic Division rivals preparing to face each other. Why Hagel Says Kucherov’s Situation Is Different The biggest distinction involves the players’ contractual circumstances and their willingness to continue playing. Kucherov is entering the final season of his eight-year contract with Tampa Bay, and he has requested a trade following unsuccessful negotiations over an extension. Unlike Larkin, however, Kucherov has indicated that he intends to continue playing for the Lightning while his situation remains unresolved. In his explanation of the trade request , Kucherov said the disagreement involved communication and respect rather than money. Hagel defended his teammate’s dedication to the organization, emphasizing that Kucherov remains committed to helping Tampa Bay win despite his uncertain future. That appears to be the point Hagel was trying to make: requesting a trade and refusing to play while waiting for one are two very different decisions. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. item.title: Ankeny Christian returns to state volleyball tournament with a victory
item.description: CORALVILLE ― Coach Michele Quick and Ankeny Christian started the 2026 state volleyball tournament the way they left it in 2024. The Eagles (38-2) beat West Monona 25-16, 25-19, 25-19 on Nov. 3 to advance to the Class 1A semifinals. Ankeny Christian missed the state tournament a season ago, and 1A teams got a break from seeing Eagles consistently dominate the field. "It's pretty exciting to be back," Quick said. "We knew we had a lot of potential this year, and we had a lot of pieces that we needed as far as our offense, and we have some great defense behind our offense as well. So it's pretty exciting. We have some new girls that haven't been here before, but we definitely have some experienced girls too." After a season of regrouping, a school-record 35 regular-season wins, a 7-0 conference mark and five regular-season tournament wins, the Eagles are primed to get a fourth state title in five seasons. The Eagles put together an impressive regular-season resume with wins over North Polk, Aplington-Parkersburg, Denver and Grundy Center. The only losses all season were against 5A Ankeny and 3A Roland-Story, two teams that also qualified for the state tournament. West Monona battled in the early parts of each set Tuesday night. In the first set, Breeze Bentz kept Ankeny Christian afloat. Her kill from the right side made the score 14-10. A play later another kill from Bentz gave the Eagles a five-point cushion. The second set was an even stronger fight from the Spartans, and Ankeny Christian didn't pull away until late in the game. Havanna Dolbeare added to her kill total and gave the Eagles the 25-19 win. In the third set, West Monona got within two, 15-13, but the more disciplined Ankeny Christian team used its service game and attacking to win and end the night. "I feel like we just focus on the next point," Dolbeare said. "We don't think about all the mistakes we made in the past. We let those go, and we just focus on the next point, and we lock in from there." Dolbeare and Bentz combined for 32 kills, and setter Gabbie Quick assisted 30 times in the win. Dani Craighead and Gabbie Quick are freshman starters. Dolbeare and Karmen Lamberts are sophomore starters. Bentz is a junior, as is fellow starter Liv Nehring. Libero Katelyn Weathers is the only senior starter. "We are just such an exciting group," Weathers said. "We have fun, and right now we are just taking everything one point at a time. It's really, really important that we come out strong, and even if we don't and we are stuck in a rut, we want to come out and stay high." (Photo by Oliver McKenna/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The College Football Rankings debuted tonight. And predictably, they stirred up quite a bit of controversy. There’s no doubt the SEC’s lobbying this offseason made a positive impact for them, as 10 of their teams were ranked in this week’s edition. Closer to home, all eyes were on which Group of 6 team would be selected, where they’d rank, and whether there would be multiple G6 teams. All of those questions were answered tonight, although some of those answers were less than ideal. If the College Football Playoff started today, Boise State would be the Group of 6 representative, as they were the highest-ranked G6 team. However, they were ranked 25th, a few spots lower than their rankings in the Coaches and AP Polls. Coming in at no. 25 #BleedBlue | #BuiltDifferent pic.twitter.com/40K4zkxfMD — Boise State Football (@BroncoSportsFB) November 4, 2026 Ranking the Broncos 25th, behind two three-loss teams, sends a clear message. Group of 6 teams should just be thankful to be included at all. And also, it’s most likely a protective measure to ensure they don’t rise too high over the next few weeks and accidentally get a first-round bye or home game, like they did two years ago. Obviously, Boise State would be a huge underdog and, at this point, be the 12-seed, which would match them up with Alabama. item.title: Ben Johnson Opens Up on Feeling Jeffery Simmons’ Presence in His Bears Debut
item.description: Jeffery Simmons has played his first game for the Chicago Bears , and helped them to secure an important win. The franchise beat the Seattle Seahawks, the defending Super Bowl champions, with a score of 17-34. The dominating victory has improved the team’s current record to 6 wins and 2 losses. Simmons has arrived mid-season from the Tennessee Titans, and already had a great impact in his first game. He got much praise from head coach Ben Johnson as well. Ben Johnson praises Jeffery Simmons Simmons made an immediate impact in his Bears debut over the Seahawks at Lumen Field. He was acquired from the Titans five days earlier in a trade that sent Chicago’s 2027 and 2028 first-round picks plus a 2027 fourth-round selection in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-rounder. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle recorded six tackles (tied for the team lead), one sack, two tackles for loss, one pass deflection, and multiple quarterback pressures while playing 48 snaps. His highlight of the game was sacking Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold, his first for the team since arriving. According to the ESPN broadcast , the Bears allowed just 2.3 yards per play with Simmons on the field. In the post game press conference, Johnson praised the defensive tackle. He said , “He’s fit right in. You can feel his presence out there, whether it’s during the play or even after. You can feel him talking smack, which I think elevates everyone. To come in there and have a share of the lead in tackles and a sack in his first game, his impact was profound.” Simmons also talked about his performance afterwards. Jeffery Simmons addresses debut game Simmons addressed his performance in his first game for the Bears. He said , “If you block me one-on-one, I need to win the one-on-one. If I don’t win a one-on-one, the coaches should be on me. I hold myself to a high standard. It felt great to get my first sack as a Chicago Bear in my first game.” He added, “If I’m getting a double team, I expect them to win their single block. We don’t need to blitz. I feel like if we can win at the line of scrimmage without the blitzes, that makes the guys’ jobs on the back end that much easier.” Jeffery Simmons and the Chicago Bears will now prepare for the next game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. item.title: Misfortune, Not Miscues, Led to Flyers’ Loss vs. Wild
item.description: PHILADELPHIA – It was misfortune, not miscues, that led to the Philadelphia Flyers (4-9-4) 4-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild (11-3-3) on Tuesday at Xfinity Mobile Arena. The Flyers played hard, and well at that, but in the end, they lost to the better. Matt Boldy, Michael McCarron, Joel Eriksson Ek, and Danila Yurov scored for the Wild. Tyson Foerster and Denver Barkey scored for the Flyers. If you erase 30 seconds from the first period, it was actually a pretty even first 20 minutes. However, the score will tell you otherwise. Less than five minutes into the game, the Wild scored twice in the span of 31 seconds, giving them a commanding lead. The first goal came from Matt Boldy, and yeah, it came from blown coverage. But when you have Boldy, Quinn Hughes , Kirill Kaprizov , and Joel Eriksson Ek dancing around the zone, it’s hard to contain. Hughes had an effortless setup, and Boldy did not miss. The second goal came off a flukey bounce off Porter Martone ’s skate, but Michael McCarron was in the right place to bury the puck. The rest of the period was pretty even. It was just a bad 31 seconds; that wasn’t even all that bad. Philly managed to fight back in the shot battle, going into the first intermission down 2-0, but only down 8-7 in shots. Period No. 2 got off to an unfortunate start. Another tough break for the Flyers, as Jamie Drysdale’s attempt to clear the zone was stopped by an official, keeping it in play for the Wild, who scored soon after courtesy of Joel Eriksson Ek. It was misfortune, not miscues, that put Philly down 3-0 early in the 2nd period. Regardless, they weren’t getting any offense to help dig out of the hole. The Flyers got on the board in the latter half of the period after a great play by Matvei Michkov to settle play down. He found Jamie Drysdale, who put the puck on the money, finding Tyson Foerster’s stick in the slot, who redirected it past Jesper Wallstedt to get the Flyers on the board. Ideally, the Flyers would have tacked on another to have a good chance at fighting back. They had their chances, but could not convert. So, they went into the second intermission trailing 3-1, and being outshot by the Wild 18-14. They found that ideal start in the third period, however, as a penalty drawn by Travis Konecny led to an early-period power play. Denver Barkey capitalized on the chance, bringing the Flyers within a goal with plenty of time to go. Philly was putting the pressure on Minnesota, racking up shots while holding the Wild without one for the first 9 minutes of the period. The Wild picked up the pressure, but the Flyers were still playing well. In the end, the Flyers played really well against the Wild, but ran out of time. Despite the comeback effort, they simply ran out of time. The Flyers pulled Dan Vladar, but could not score at 6-on-5. Danila Yurov scored on the empty net, sealing the 4-2 win for the Wild. item.title: How confident are you in the Bears and in Caleb Williams moving forward?
item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) calls a play at the line of scrimmage against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. The Chicago Bears have won three straight games in the most impressive fashion imaginable. Caleb Williams is the 1st quarterback in Bears history to lead his team to 30+ points in three consecutive games with no turnovers. The Bears also never trailed in any of these three games, and that 3-game streak of scoring 30 points while never trailing is tied for the second-longest streak in franchise history . They went four in a row three times, all in the 1940s (1941, 1942, and 1948). Those teams were led by Hall of Fame quarterback Sid Luckman, who is the only quarterback to win a league MVP for the Bears. There was some buzz around Williams as an MVP candidate before the season, and that was amplified following the Bears’ 59-point explosion in Week 1, but the hamstring injury seemed to derail that because it kept him out of the next three games. In his weekly NFL MVP Tracker at NFL.com , Kevin Patra wrote about the historical unlikelihood of Williams winning it. In the post NFL-AFL merger era (since 1970) in non-strike-shortened seasons, only one player has missed three games and still won the NFL MVP award: Joe Montana in 1989. Cool Joe battled through various injuries that season, missing Weeks 6, 8, and 15, and portions of others. While a long shot, the Bears did just beat last year’s Super Bowl participants in back-to-back weeks on primetime. They also have three more stand-alone games on the schedule, including a third straight primetime affair this Sunday. item.title: AEK Athens: The club with Real Madrid in their anthem
item.description: Real Madrid's Brazilian , Ronaldo (C) fights for the ball with AEK Athens Nikolaos Kostenoglou (R), under the eyes of Konstantinos Katsouranis during their Champion's League match in Madrid 22 October 2002. AFP PHOTO/Pierre-Philippe MARCOU (Photo by Pierre-Philippe MARCOU / AFP) (Photo by PIERRE-PHILIPPE MARCOU/AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images AEK Athens have been singing about Real Madrid for more than half a century, thanks to a friendly draw and a forward who also recorded the club’s anthem. The line translates roughly as “And your name became the terror of Real.” Its origins lie in Madrid’s visit to Nea Filadelfeia on May 12, 1965, when the teams drew 3–3. Ferenc Puskás featured for Madrid, but AEK’s Mimis Papaioannou caught the visitors’ attention in that game. Puskás was sufficiently impressed to want Papaioannou at Real Madrid. According to Giannis Lambiris’s report for SPORT24, which reproduced the forward’s recollections from an interview with Kathimerini journalist Christos Kontos, Puskás approached him at a dinner hosted by AEK for Madrid’s delegation. He praised Papaioannou’s ability, told him Madrid would sign him, and offered advice on improving his movement without the ball. Madrid’s interest developed into an offer, but AEK refused to let him leave. AEK recalled his performance in a 2021 anniversary post, describing the match as the inspiration for their anthem. Greek broadcaster Sport FM reproduced the club’s account. Papaioannou later provided the vocals for the recording. According to a Greek publication, in.gr, the song began taking shape in 1965 during a tour of Germany involving the footballer and singer Stelios Kazantzidis. The publication credits Christos Kolokotronis with the lyrics and Kazantzidis with the music, and reports that the anthem was recorded and adopted in 1971. The dates rule out a common assumption that the Madrid reference came from AEK’s better-known European results against them. AEK won 1–0 in Athens in the first leg of their 1985 UEFA Cup tie, before Madrid overturned the deficit with a 5–0 home victory. Their Champions League meetings in 2002 were closer. Madrid recovered from 3–1 down to draw in Athens, while AEK came from two goals behind to earn a 2–2 draw at the Bernabéu.

(Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) LATHAM - Abigail Meissner had the game on her foot, but the ghost of what happened nine minutes earlier was playing in the back of her head. The Averill Park sophomore had already gotten one chance to give the Golden Knights a Section 2 Class A girls' soccer championship with an overtime winner against Schalmont, but that shot smacked off the goalpost. Meissner controlled the ball 40 yards from the goal and dribbled through multiple defenders before neatly finishing past Schalmont goalkeeper Mandee Banks, giving Averill Park a 4-3 overtime win and the program its first sectional title since 2018, while also putting an end to a run of six straight area championships for Schalmont. "I was crying, and everybody just tackled me," Meissner said of the scene after her winning goal. "I was so excited and happy." The sophomore's game-winner ended a rollercoaster ride of a championship game. Teagan DeLair scored twice and assisted on a Mia Viloria goal as No. 2 seed Averill Park (7-9-3 overall) built a 3-1 lead with 30 minutes to play.
